title: Translation and cross-cultural adaptation of EAT-26 questionnaire in Urdu
author: Jamil, Zahid, et al.

steps.title: Forward translation of EAT-26
steps.instruction: Two independent native‑Urdu, English‑fluent translators each produce a forward translation of the English EAT‑26 instructions, statements, and response choices into Urdu.

steps.title: Create pooled translation and assess equivalence
steps.instruction: Translators and the local coordinator reach consensus to produce a pooled Urdu version; developmental experts review it for conceptual, content, semantic, and technical equivalence, recording all suggested changes in cultural adaptation grids.

steps.title: Conduct cognitive interviews
steps.instruction: Train the adaptation team to perform cognitive interviews using paraphrasing, debriefing, and probing techniques with a prepared interview guide containing probes (e.g., “Can you explain what you have understood by this question?” etc.). Conduct interviews with three focus‑group sets: two groups of university‑going native‑Urdu girls (mixed Potohari/Urdu, total n = 12, 4 per group) and one group with a female clinician (n = 2).

substeps.instruction: Train interviewers on paraphrasing, debriefing, probing methods.
Prepare cognitive interview guide with standard probes.
Run focus‑group interviews with the described participant groups.

steps.title: Finalize tool via modification grids
steps.instruction: Compile findings from each interview into technical modification grids, discuss the grids with an expert panel, revise the Urdu EAT‑26 accordingly, and repeat interviews with successive target groups until no new issues emerge and participants are clear on all items.

steps.title: Backward translation and comparison
steps.instruction: An independent bilingual public‑health consultant back‑translates the Urdu version into English without being given the original questionnaire name; the focus is on conceptual equivalence, not linguistic detail. The team lead then compares the back‑translation with the original English EAT‑26 to identify misunderstandings, mistranslations, or inaccuracies and prepares the final pre‑test tool.

steps.title: Pre‑test questionnaire with adolescents
steps.instruction: Administer the finalized Urdu questionnaire to five adolescent girls (three university students and two clinic attendees) to assess appropriateness, comprehension, and administration time.

steps.title: Proofread final Urdu version
steps.instruction: Proofread the final Urdu questionnaire to correct any typing or spelling errors before release.
